options: Throws, because the sequence has more than one element
questions.explanation: `SingleOrDefault()` returns the default only when the sequence is empty; it throws if there is more than one element.
Index 10 is out of range, and `ElementAtOrDefault()` returns the default value in that case, which is `0` for `int`. `ElementAt()` would throw instead.

questions.prompt: `mixed` is an `IEnumerable<object>` holding `1`, `"a"` and `2`. How do `mixed.OfType<int>()` and `mixed.Cast<int>()` differ?
options: Both yield 1 and 2 and silently skip `"a"`
questions.explanation: `OfType<TResult>()` keeps only elements assignable to the type and skips others silently, while `Cast<TResult>()` assumes every element can be cast and throws `InvalidCastException` if one can't.

questions.prompt: You need to index numbers by an `"Even"`/`"Odd"` key, so many elements share each key. Which conversion fits?
questions.explanation: `ToLookup()` allows multiple values per key and doesn't throw on duplicate keys; `ToDictionary()` throws an exception if duplicate keys exist.
